newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice brings separate discrimination cases.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice brings separate discrimination cases.

text.p: In separate cases, the Justice Department said four Georgia men were arrested Wednesday for plotting to set a black couple's home on fire, and it sued an Ohio nursing home for discriminating against blacks.

The defendants in the Georgia case were charged with violating federal criminal civil rights laws by conspiring to burn a trailer home in Telfair County in an effort to scare away the owners, department officials said.
The indictment charged that one defendant, Razell Spires, in April offered to pay $500 to anyone who would burn the trailer home.

The other three defendants, Joey Spires, Mac Rainey and Tommy Hulett, went to the trailer and started a fire, according to the indictment. The three allegedly then discussed ways to conceal their involvement in the scheme.
No was was hurt in the incident.
In the Ohio case the Justice Department said it had brought the first housing discrimination lawsuit against a nursing home, charging that a facility in Akron refused to rent rooms to blacks.

The department's civil rights division said the lawsuit charged the Lorantffy Care Centre engaged in an unlawful pattern of discrimination against blacks by falsely telling prospective residents rooms were unavailable.

"All potential residents of nursing homes should be treated fairly and given correct information about housing availability, Acting Assistant Attorney General Isabelle Katz Pinzler said in a statement.

The case stemmed from a Justice Department investigation in which blacks and whites posed as relatives seeking information about the availability of nursing home rooms for elderly family members. Blacks were turned down while whites were told rooms were available, department officials said.

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Cleveland, sought an order barring the nursing home, its management and certain employees any further discrimination. It also sought unspecified damages and civil penalties.
